title: Splitting water with a battery
body: Priya fits two carbon electrodes through rubber stoppers at the base of a plastic mug and connects them to a 6 volt battery. She fills the mug with water, adds a few drops of dilute sulphuric acid, and inverts two test tubes filled with water over the electrodes. When the current is switched on, bubbles form at both electrodes and push the water out of the test tubes. After some time she notices that one test tube has collected about twice as much gas as the other. Her teacher then brings a burning candle near the mouth of each test tube in turn.
